info.name: Fake Store API
info.description:
# Manual QA API Testing Portfolio

## Overview

This collection demonstrates Manual QA API testing skills using the Fake Store API.

It includes functional and negative testing scenarios designed to validate API behavior, response structure, business rules, and error handling.

## Features

- Functional API Testing
    
- Negative Testing
    
- JSON Schema Validation (AJV)
    
- Business Rule Validation
    
- Response Time (SLA) Validation
    
- Collection & Environment Variables
    
- Request Chaining
    
- Reusable Test Scripts
    

## Technologies

- Postman
    
- JavaScript
    
- AJV
    
- JSON Schema
    
- REST APIs
    

## Note

The Fake Store API is a public mock API intended for learning purposes. Some negative scenarios do not follow standard REST API behavior (for example, invalid resource identifiers may return HTTP 200 OK with an empty response body). These cases have been documented throughout the collection.

---

**Author:** Karen Romero

item.name: ❌ Negative

exec: pm.test("Fake Store API returns an empty response body", () => {
"Production APIs should reject invalid Product IDs with HTTP 400 or 404. Fake Store API returns HTTP 200 with an empty response body."

request.description:
Purpose

Verify that the API correctly handles requests where the Product ID path parameter contains an invalid data type (string instead of integer).

Expected Behavior (Production API)

• HTTP 400 Bad Request or HTTP 404 Not Found.  
• A descriptive error message should be returned.  
• No product data should be exposed.  
• The API should not generate an internal server error.

Observed Behavior (Fake Store API)

The Fake Store API returns HTTP 200 OK with an empty response body instead of rejecting the request. This behavior is acceptable for this mock API but would typically be considered a defect in a production REST API.

Business Risk

Accepting invalid identifiers may hide client-side implementation errors and makes API behavior inconsistent and difficult to troubleshoot.

request.description:
## Purpose

Verify that the API correctly handles requests using a negative Product ID.

## Expected Behavior (Production API)

- Return HTTP 400 Bad Request or HTTP 404 Not Found.
    
- Return a descriptive error message.
    
- No product information should be returned.
    
- The request should be handled gracefully without server errors.
    

## Observed Behavior (Fake Store API)

The Fake Store API returns HTTP 200 OK with an empty response body instead of rejecting the request.

## Business Risk

Accepting invalid identifiers may hide client-side validation issues and lead to inconsistent API behavior.

exec: pm.test("Response was handled by the API", () => {

request.description:
## Purpose

Verify the API behavior when requesting a product that does not exist.

## Expected Behavior (Production API)

- Return HTTP 404 Not Found.
    
- Return a descriptive error message indicating that the resource was not found.
    
- Do not expose internal implementation details.
    

## Observed Behavior

The response depends on the API implementation. The purpose of this test is to verify that the API handles nonexistent resources consistently.

## Business Risk

Returning incorrect responses for nonexistent resources may confuse API consumers and complicate client-side error handling.

## Purpose

Verify that the API validates required request fields when creating a product.

## Expected Behavior (Production API)

- Return HTTP 400 Bad Request or HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity.
    
- Return a descriptive validation error.
    
- The product should not be created.
    

## Observed Behavior (Fake Store API)

The Fake Store API may accept the request despite the missing required field because it is a mock API.

## Business Risk

Missing required information may result in incomplete or inconsistent data being stored.

## Purpose

Verify that the API rejects invalid data types.

## Expected Behavior (Production API)

- Return HTTP 400 Bad Request or HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity.
    
- The product should not be created.
    

## Observed Behavior (Fake Store API)

The API may accept the request because it performs little or no input validation.

## Business Risk

Accepting incorrect data types may cause application errors and inconsistent data.

## Purpose

Verify that the API validates empty request bodies.

## Expected Behavior (Production API)

- Return HTTP 400 Bad Request.
    
- Return a validation error indicating missing required fields.
    

## Observed Behavior (Fake Store API)

The API may still accept the request because it is intended for demonstration purposes.

## Business Risk

Processing empty payloads may generate invalid records.

## Purpose

Verify that the API validates the Content-Type request header.

## Expected Behavior (Production API)

- Return HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type.
    
- Reject the request.
    

## Observed Behavior (Fake Store API)

The API may still process the request despite the incorrect Content-Type.

## Business Risk

Ignoring Content-Type validation may allow malformed or unexpected payloads.

exec: pm.test("Response body contains an error message", () => {

request.description:
## Purpose

Verify that the API correctly rejects unsupported HTTP methods.

## Request

PATCH /products

## Expected Behavior (Production API)

A REST API should reject unsupported HTTP methods by returning:

- HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed
    
- A descriptive error message
    
- Information about the supported methods (optional)
    

## Observed Behavior (Fake Store API)

The API rejects the request and returns an HTML error page with the following message:

"Cannot PATCH /products"

Although the response body is HTML instead of JSON, the API correctly indicates that the PATCH method is not supported for this endpoint.

## Business Risk

Returning inconsistent error formats (HTML instead of JSON) makes it more difficult for API consumers to parse and handle errors consistently.

item.description:
# Negative Testing

These requests validate how the API behaves when invalid input is provided.

The objective is to verify that invalid requests are handled gracefully and consistently.

Examples include:

- Invalid Product IDs
    
- Invalid HTTP Methods
    
- Missing Required Fields
    
- Invalid Data Types
    
- Invalid Content-Type
    
- Empty Request Body
    

Some scenarios document differences between the Fake Store API behavior and production REST API best practices.

# Products

This folder contains all API tests related to Product resources.

The requests are organized into:

- Positive Testing
    
- Negative Testing
    

The objective is to validate API functionality, business rules, response schemas, and error handling.
